title: Emotions and reactions + present subjunctive (me alegra que)
micro_note: Any verb of emotion, surprise, or regret (alegrarse de, temer, sentir, sorprender, dar pena) requires subjunctive in the subordinate que-clause with a different subject.
contrast_a: Me alegra que estés aquí hoy.
contrast_a_en: I am glad that you are here today.
contrast_b: Siento mucho que no puedan venir.
contrast_b_en: I am very sorry they cannot come.

title: Value judgments + subjunctive (es lógico/raro/injusto que)
micro_note: Value judgments with ser/parecer + adjective + que (es bueno, es raro, es increíble, me parece justo) trigger subjunctive, unlike certainty phrases (es verdad/evidente que).
contrast_a: Es raro que no haya contestado.
contrast_a_en: It is strange that he hasn't replied.
contrast_b: Es evidente que sabe la respuesta.
contrast_b_en: It is obvious that she knows the answer.

title: Doubt and denial + subjunctive (dudar que, no creer que)
micro_note: Affirmative creer/pensar/parecer take indicative; negated (no creo que, no parece que) or explicit doubt (dudo que, niego que) switches to subjunctive.
contrast_a: Creo que tienen razón.
contrast_a_en: I think they are right.
contrast_b: No creo que tengan razón.
contrast_b_en: I don't think they are right.

title: Advice, prohibition, and permission (aconsejar, prohibir, permitir)
micro_note: Influence verbs like recomendar, aconsejar, pedir, exigir, prohibir, and dejar take indirect pronoun + que + subjunctive (or infinitive for recomendar/permitir).
contrast_a: Te aconsejo que revises el texto.
contrast_a_en: I advise you to review the text.
contrast_b: Prohíben que se fume en el patio.
contrast_b_en: They forbid smoking in the courtyard.

title: Purpose clauses with para que + subjunctive
micro_note: Use para + infinitive for same subject, but switch to para que + subjunctive whenever the second clause introduces a different subject.
contrast_a: Te lo repito para que lo entiendas.
contrast_a_en: I repeat it to you so that you understand it.
contrast_b: Abrí la ventana para que entrara aire.
contrast_b_en: I opened the window so air would come in.

title: Temporal clauses with antes de que + subjunctive (always)
micro_note: Antes de que ALWAYS takes the subjunctive—even in the past—because the second action had not yet occurred relative to the first.
contrast_a: Salgamos antes de que anochezca.
contrast_a_en: Let's leave before night falls.
contrast_b: Terminó antes de que llegáramos.
contrast_b_en: She finished before we arrived.

title: Temporal clauses with hasta que, en cuanto, tan pronto como
micro_note: These time conjunctions take indicative for completed past or habitual facts, and subjunctive whenever pointing to a pending future moment.
contrast_a: Esperé hasta que llegó el tren.
contrast_a_en: I waited until the train arrived.
contrast_b: Esperaré hasta que llegue el tren.
contrast_b_en: I will wait until the train arrives.

title: Subjunctive in relative clauses with unknown antecedents
micro_note: Use indicative in a relative clause when the thing exists and is known; switch to subjunctive when seeking something hypothetical, unspecified, or nonexistent.
contrast_a: Busco un piso que tiene balcón.
contrast_a_en: I am looking for a specific flat that has a balcony.
contrast_b: Busco un piso que tenga balcón.
contrast_b_en: I am looking for any flat that has a balcony.

title: Subjunctive after negative antecedents (no hay nadie que...)
micro_note: When the main clause denies existence (no hay nadie que, no conozco ningún sitio que), the relative clause always takes the subjunctive.
contrast_a: No hay nadie que sepa ese secreto.
contrast_a_en: There is nobody who knows that secret.
contrast_b: No encontré nada que me convenciera.
contrast_b_en: I found nothing that convinced me.

title: Present perfect subjunctive (haya + participio)
micro_note: Use haya/hayas/haya/hayamos/hayáis/hayan + past participle in subjunctive triggers when the subordinate action is already completed or recent.
contrast_a: Espero que hayas descansado bien.
contrast_a_en: I hope you have rested well.
contrast_b: Dudo que hayan recibido el paquete.
contrast_b_en: I doubt they have received the package.

title: Concessive aunque + indicative (known fact) vs subjunctive (hypothetical)
micro_note: Aunque + indicative states a known obstacle ('even though it is raining'). Aunque + subjunctive treats it as uncertain or irrelevant ('even if it rains').
contrast_a: Salimos aunque llueve fuerte.
contrast_a_en: We are going out even though it's raining hard.
contrast_b: Saldremos aunque llueva fuerte.
contrast_b_en: We will go out even if it rains hard.

title: Conditional conjunctions a menos que / sin que / siempre que
micro_note: A menos que ('unless'), sin que ('without'), con tal de que ('provided that'), and en caso de que ALWAYS require the subjunctive.
contrast_a: Iremos al parque a menos que llueva.
contrast_a_en: We will go to the park unless it rains.
contrast_b: Salió sin que nadie lo notara.
contrast_b_en: He left without anyone noticing.

title: Quizá / tal vez + subjunctive vs indicative
micro_note: Quizá(s), tal vez, and posiblemente take subjunctive for stronger doubt and indicative for higher certainty—only when placed BEFORE the verb.
contrast_a: Quizá venga mañana con nosotros.
contrast_a_en: Perhaps she might come with us tomorrow.
contrast_b: Tal vez ya saben la noticia.
contrast_b_en: Maybe they already know the news.

title: Imperfect subjunctive formation (-ra / -se from ellos preterite)
micro_note: Take the ellos preterite (hablaron, tuvieron, dijeron), drop -ron, and add -ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -rais, -ran. Always accent the vowel before -ramos.
contrast_a: Quiero que vengas pronto.
contrast_a_en: I want you to come soon.
contrast_b: Quería que vinieras pronto.
contrast_b_en: I wanted you to come soon.

title: Second conditional: Si + imperfect subjunctive, conditional
micro_note: Express unreal or unlikely present/future hypotheses using si + imperfect subjunctive (-ra) and the simple conditional (-ía) in the main clause.
contrast_a: Si tuviera tiempo, aprendería piano.
contrast_a_en: If I had time, I would learn piano.
contrast_b: Si viviera allí, caminaría al mar.
contrast_b_en: If I lived there, I would walk to the sea.

title: Como si + imperfect subjunctive ('as if')
micro_note: Como si ALWAYS triggers a past subjunctive (imperfect or pluperfect), never present subjunctive or indicative, because it presents an unreal comparison.
contrast_a: Habla como si supiera todo.
contrast_a_en: He talks as if he knew everything.
contrast_b: Me miró como si no me conociera.
contrast_b_en: She looked at me as if she didn't know me.

title: Polite softening with quisiera / pudiera / debiera
micro_note: The -ra imperfect subjunctive of querer, poder, and deber acts as an ultra-polite alternative to the conditional in formal requests.
contrast_a: Quisiera hablar con el gerente.
contrast_a_en: I would like to speak with the manager.
contrast_b: ¿Pudiera confirmarme la fecha?
contrast_b_en: Could you confirm the date for me?

title: No es que + subjunctive, sino que + indicative
micro_note: Deny one explanation using no es que + subjunctive, then supply the true reason with sino que + indicative.
contrast_a: No es que esté enfadado, sino que estoy cansado.
contrast_a_en: It's not that I'm angry, it's that I'm tired.
contrast_b: No es que no quiera ir, sino que trabajo.
contrast_b_en: It's not that I don't want to go, it's that I'm working.

title: Backshifting tenses in past indirect speech (dijo que...)
micro_note: After a past reporting verb (dijo, explicó, contó), backshift: present->imperfect, preterite/perfect->pluperfect, future->conditional, imperative->imperfect subjunctive.
contrast_a: Dijo: «Llegaré a las ocho».
contrast_a_en: He said: 'I will arrive at eight.'
contrast_b: Dijo que llegaría a las ocho.
contrast_b_en: He said he would arrive at eight.

title: Reporting commands with decir/pedir que + imperfect subjunctive
micro_note: When reporting an order or request in the past, replace the imperative with pedir/decir/ordenar que + imperfect subjunctive.
contrast_a: Me dijo: «Cierra la puerta».
contrast_a_en: She told me: 'Close the door.'
contrast_b: Me dijo que cerrara la puerta.
contrast_b_en: She told me to close the door.

title: Shifting time and space deixis in reported speech
micro_note: In past indirect speech, shift pointers to the narrator's perspective: hoy->ese día, mañana->al día siguiente, ayer->el día anterior, aquí->allí.
contrast_a: Prometió: «Volveré mañana».
contrast_a_en: He promised: 'I will return tomorrow.'
contrast_b: Prometió que volvería al día siguiente.
contrast_b_en: He promised he would return the next day.

title: Future perfect (habré + participio) for completion and past guess
micro_note: Use future haber + past participle either for actions completed before a future deadline or to speculate about a recent past event ('must have').
contrast_a: Para junio habré acabado el curso.
contrast_a_en: By June I will have finished the course.
contrast_b: ¿Por qué no vino? Habrá perdido el tren.
contrast_b_en: Why didn't he come? He must have missed the train.

title: Conditional of probability in the past ('was probably')
micro_note: Just as simple future speculates about the present, simple conditional speculates about an imperfect past state ('it was probably around ten').
contrast_a: Serían las diez cuando volvió.
contrast_a_en: It was probably around ten when she returned.
contrast_b: Tendría unos veinte años entonces.
contrast_b_en: He must have been about twenty back then.

title: Process passive with ser + participio + por
micro_note: Formal and journalistic Spanish forms process passives with ser (any tense) + agreeing past participle + por for the agent.
contrast_a: El puente fue diseñado por un equipo local.
contrast_a_en: The bridge was designed by a local team.
contrast_b: La ley será aprobada la próxima semana.
contrast_b_en: The law will be passed next week.

title: Impersonal se + a + person (no plural verb agreement)
micro_note: With human direct objects preceded by personal a, impersonal se stays strictly third-person singular even if the object is plural.
contrast_a: Se busca a los testigos del accidente.
contrast_a_en: Witnesses of the accident are being sought.
contrast_b: Se entrevistó a veinte candidatos.
contrast_b_en: Twenty candidates were interviewed.

title: Ir + gerundio for gradual progression
micro_note: Ir + gerundio highlights an action unfolding bit by bit over time ('gradually getting better / learning step by step').
contrast_a: Voy entendiendo mejor el acento.
contrast_a_en: I am gradually understanding the accent better.
contrast_b: La sala se fue llenando poco a poco.
contrast_b_en: The hall gradually filled up.

title: Venir + gerundio for ongoing trend up to now
micro_note: Venir + gerundio traces an action repeating or developing from an earlier point continuously up to the present moment.
contrast_a: Vengo diciendo esto desde enero.
contrast_a_en: I have been saying this since January.
contrast_b: Los precios vienen subiendo todo el año.
contrast_b_en: Prices have been rising all year.

title: Andar + gerundio for intermittent/aimless ongoing activity
micro_note: Andar + gerundio conveys doing something on and off, going around doing it, or slight colloquial exasperation.
contrast_a: Anda buscando piso por el sur.
contrast_a_en: She's been going around looking for a flat down south.
contrast_b: Siempre andan quejándose del ruido.
contrast_b_en: They are always going around complaining about noise.

title: Ponerse a / echarse a + infinitive for sudden onset
micro_note: Ponerse a + infinitive starts an intentional activity; echarse a + infinitive expresses sudden bursts (reír, llorar, correr).
contrast_a: Nos pusimos a ordenar la cocina.
contrast_a_en: We set to tidying the kitchen.
contrast_b: Al oír el chiste se echó a reír.
contrast_b_en: Upon hearing the joke he burst out laughing.

title: Llegar a + infinitive ('manage to / even go so far as')
micro_note: Llegar a + infinitive marks reaching a culmination after effort or surprisingly reaching an extreme degree.
contrast_a: Llegó a dirigir toda la orquesta.
contrast_a_en: She eventually came to conduct the whole orchestra.
contrast_b: Nunca llegué a conocer a mi abuelo.
contrast_b_en: I never got to meet my grandfather.

title: Acabar / terminar + gerundio ('end up doing')
micro_note: Acabar or terminar + gerundio expresses an unexpected final outcome ('ended up doing'), distinct from terminar de + infinitive ('finished doing').
contrast_a: Acabamos cenando en un bar pequeño.
contrast_a_en: We ended up having dinner in a small bar.
contrast_b: Terminó aceptando la propuesta.
contrast_b_en: He ended up accepting the proposal.

title: Quedar en + infinitive ('agree to / arrange to')
micro_note: Quedar en + infinitive means two or more people made an agreement or plan to do something.
contrast_a: Quedamos en vernos a las siete.
contrast_a_en: We agreed to meet at seven.
contrast_b: Quedaron en repartir los gastos.
contrast_b_en: They agreed to split the expenses.

title: Llevar + past participle for accumulated progress
micro_note: Llevar + agreeing past participle counts how much of a larger task has been completed so far (always with a quantified object).
contrast_a: Llevo leídas ochenta páginas hoy.
contrast_a_en: I have read eighty pages so far today.
contrast_b: Llevamos grabados seis episodios.
contrast_b_en: We have recorded six episodes so far.

title: Tener + past participle for completed state held in hand
micro_note: Tener + agreeing past participle emphasizes the persistent state of a completed action ('have it all prepared / decided / figured out').
contrast_a: Ya tengo decidida la fecha.
contrast_a_en: I already have the date decided.
contrast_b: Tiene escritas tres novelas cortas.
contrast_b_en: She has three short novels written.

title: Preposition + el que / la que / los que / las que
micro_note: After prepositions (especially longer ones like sobre, hacia, durante), pair the definite article matching the antecedent with que.
contrast_a: La mesa sobre la que dejé el mapa.
contrast_a_en: The table on which I left the map.
contrast_b: Los temas de los que hablamos ayer.
contrast_b_en: The topics about which we spoke yesterday.

title: Non-restrictive relative clauses with commas (el cual / quien)
micro_note: Extra side information set off by commas can use el cual / la cual / quien. Never use quien in a restrictive clause without a preposition.
contrast_a: Mi tío, quien vive en Chile, nos visitó.
contrast_a_en: My uncle, who lives in Chile, visited us.
contrast_b: Llegó el informe, el cual resultó útil.
contrast_b_en: The report arrived, which proved useful.

title: Lo cual referring back to an entire clause
micro_note: Use lo cual (or lo que) after a comma to summarize and comment on the whole previous sentence ('which surprised everyone').
contrast_a: El tren salió puntual, lo cual nos alivió.
contrast_a_en: The train left on time, which relieved us.
contrast_b: No avisó antes, lo que causó retrasos.
contrast_b_en: He didn't warn ahead, which caused delays.

title: Possessive relative cuyo / cuya / cuyos / cuyas ('whose')
micro_note: Cuyo agrees in gender and number with the POSSESSED noun right after it—NOT the owner—and never takes an article.
contrast_a: Un autor cuyas novelas admiro mucho.
contrast_a_en: An author whose novels I greatly admire.
contrast_b: Una casa cuyo tejado necesita arreglos.
contrast_b_en: A house whose roof needs repairs.

title: Causal connectors como, ya que, puesto que
micro_note: Como ('since') MUST appear at the start of the sentence. Ya que and puesto que introduce known/shared reasons anywhere and take indicative.
contrast_a: Como hacía frío, cerramos la terraza.
contrast_a_en: Since it was cold, we closed the terrace.
contrast_b: Trae paraguas, ya que anuncian lluvia.
contrast_b_en: Bring an umbrella, since rain is forecast.

title: Counter-argumentative connectors sin embargo, no obstante, en cambio
micro_note: Link contrasting ideas across clauses or sentences with sin embargo / no obstante ('however') or en cambio / mientras que ('whereas').
contrast_a: El piso es pequeño; sin embargo, es luminoso.
contrast_a_en: The flat is small; however, it is bright.
contrast_b: Él prefiere montaña; ella, en cambio, playa.
contrast_b_en: He prefers mountains; she, by contrast, beaches.

title: Consecutive connectors por lo tanto, por consiguiente, de modo que
micro_note: State logical conclusions with por lo tanto or por consiguiente ('therefore'), or de modo que + indicative ('so that / with the result that').
contrast_a: Faltan datos; por lo tanto, debemos esperar.
contrast_a_en: Data is missing; therefore, we must wait.
contrast_b: Llovió todo el día, de modo que suspendimos la ruta.
contrast_b_en: It rained all day, so we called off the hike.

title: Concessive a pesar de + noun/infinitive vs a pesar de que
micro_note: Use a pesar de directly before a noun or infinitive ('despite the noise'). Add que before a conjugated verb (indicative for fact, subjunctive for hypothesis).
contrast_a: Corrió a pesar del dolor en la rodilla.
contrast_a_en: She ran despite the pain in her knee.
contrast_b: Siguió adelante a pesar de que estaba agotado.
contrast_b_en: He kept going even though he was exhausted.

title: Clausal comparisons más/menos... de lo que
micro_note: When comparing against an entire clause or expectation ('more than I thought'), replace que with de lo que (or del que / de la que for a specific noun).
contrast_a: El examen fue más fácil de lo que creía.
contrast_a_en: The exam was easier than I thought.
contrast_b: Gasta menos dinero del que gana.
contrast_b_en: She spends less money than she earns.

title: Proportional comparison cuanto más... (tanto) más
micro_note: Express 'the more X, the more Y' with cuanto más/menos + clause, más/menos + clause. Agree cuanto when placed before a noun.
contrast_a: Cuanto más practicas, mejor hablas.
contrast_a_en: The more you practice, the better you speak.
contrast_b: Cuanta menos prisa tengas, menos fallos cometerás.
contrast_b_en: The less hurry you're in, the fewer mistakes you'll make.

title: Verbs governing preposition de (acordarse de, olvidarse de, tratar de)
micro_note: Many Spanish verbs lock onto a fixed preposition: acordarse de, olvidarse de, darse cuenta de, enterarse de, enamorarse de, tratar de, depender de.
contrast_a: ¿Te acuerdas de aquel restaurante?
contrast_a_en: Do you remember that restaurant?
contrast_b: Todo depende del tiempo que haga.
contrast_b_en: Everything depends on the weather.

title: Verbs governing preposition en (pensar en, confiar en, insistir en)
micro_note: Use en with pensar en ('think about'), confiar en, creer en, consistir en, insistir en, fijarse en, and tardar en + infinitive.
contrast_a: Siempre pienso en ese viaje.
contrast_a_en: I always think about that trip.
contrast_b: Tardó diez minutos en responder.
contrast_b_en: It took him ten minutes to answer.

title: Verbs governing preposition con (soñar con, contar con, conformarse con)
micro_note: Use con with soñar con ('dream about'), contar con ('rely on'), casarse con ('marry'), encontrarse con ('run into'), and conformarse con.
contrast_a: Puedes contar conmigo para el proyecto.
contrast_a_en: You can count on me for the project.
contrast_b: Anoche soñé con mi antigua escuela.
contrast_b_en: Last night I dreamed about my old school.

title: Verbs governing preposition a (aprender a, ayudar a, dedicarse a)
micro_note: Use a before infinitives or nouns after aprender a, enseñar a, ayudar a, invitar a, acostumbrarse a, negarse a, atreverse a, and dedicarse a.
contrast_a: Me estoy acostumbrando al horario.
contrast_a_en: I am getting used to the schedule.
contrast_b: Se negó a firmar sin leer primero.
contrast_b_en: She refused to sign without reading first.

title: Verbs governing preposition por (preocuparse por, luchar por, optar por)
micro_note: Use por with preocuparse por, interesarse por, esforzarse por, optar por, and preguntar por ('ask after someone').
contrast_a: No te preocupes por ese detalle.
contrast_a_en: Don't worry about that detail.
contrast_b: Optamos por viajar en tren nocturno.
contrast_b_en: We opted to travel by night train.

title: Topicalization with redundant object pronoun (El libro lo traje yo)
micro_note: When placing a definite direct object at the front of a Spanish sentence for topic focus, you MUST insert a matching copy pronoun (lo/la/los/las) before the verb.
contrast_a: Traje las entradas ayer.
contrast_a_en: I brought the tickets yesterday.
contrast_b: Las entradas las traje ayer.
contrast_b_en: As for the tickets, I brought them yesterday.

title: Cleft focus constructions with ser (Fue Ana quien...)
micro_note: Highlight a specific element using ser + focused item + quien/el que/donde/cuando/por lo que, matching tense between both clauses.
contrast_a: Fue Marta quien encontró la llave.
contrast_a_en: It was Marta who found the key.
contrast_b: Es aquí donde empieza el sendero.
contrast_b_en: It is here where the trail begins.

title: Subjunctive with verbs of communication: statement vs command
micro_note: Decir, escribir, and insistir take indicative when reporting a fact ('he says it's cold'), but switch to subjunctive when transmitting an order ('he tells you to come').
contrast_a: Dice que la puerta está cerrada.
contrast_a_en: He says that the door is closed.
contrast_b: Dice que cierres la puerta.
contrast_b_en: He says for you to close the door.

title: Sentir vs sentir que / temer vs temerse que nuance
micro_note: Sentir + indicative means 'notice/feel physically'; sentir + subjunctive means 'regret'. Temerse (reflexive) often softens bad news with indicative or subjunctive.
contrast_a: Siento que hace más frío hoy.
contrast_a_en: I feel that it is colder today.
contrast_b: Siento que no hayas podido venir.
contrast_b_en: I am sorry that you couldn't come.

title: Indefinite reduplication (sea lo que sea, pase lo que pase)
micro_note: Double a present subjunctive verb around a relative word (vaya donde vaya, digan lo que digan, cueste lo que cueste) to express 'no matter what/where'.
contrast_a: Pase lo que pase, te apoyaré.
contrast_a_en: No matter what happens, I will support you.
contrast_b: Cueste lo que cueste, lo lograremos.
contrast_b_en: Whatever it takes, we will achieve it.

title: Por más / por mucho que + subjunctive ('no matter how much')
micro_note: Por mucho/más + (noun/adj) + que takes subjunctive for future/uncertain effort and indicative for known repeated past facts.
contrast_a: Por mucho que insistas, no cambiará.
contrast_a_en: No matter how much you insist, it won't change.
contrast_b: Por más que buscaba, no lo encontraba.
contrast_b_en: No matter how hard I looked, I couldn't find it.

title: Ethical / sympathetic dative (se me / te me / no me llores)
micro_note: Spanish adds an extra indirect pronoun (me, te, nos) to show emotional involvement or personal stake in an event ('my child won't eat for me').
contrast_a: El niño no come nada hoy.
contrast_a_en: The child isn't eating anything today.
contrast_b: El niño no me come nada hoy.
contrast_b_en: My child won't eat a thing for me today.

title: Nosotros commands (¡Hablemos! / ¡Vámonos!)
micro_note: Form 'let's...' commands with the nosotros present subjunctive (comamos, salgamos). With reflexive nos, drop the final -s before attaching nos (sentémonos, vámonos).
contrast_a: Empecemos antes de que sea tarde.
contrast_a_en: Let's start before it gets late.
contrast_b: Vámonos ya que cierra el metro.
contrast_b_en: Let's head out now before the subway closes.

title: Imperative + pronouns: affirmative enclitic vs negative proclitic
micro_note: Attach pronouns directly to the END of affirmative commands (dímelo, siéntate), adding an accent; place pronouns BEFORE negative commands (no me lo digas).
contrast_a: Cuéntamelo todo sin prisa.
contrast_a_en: Tell me everything without rushing.
contrast_b: No me lo cuentes todavía.
contrast_b_en: Don't tell me yet.

title: Adverbial gerund for manner, instrument, and condition
micro_note: A bare gerund modifies the main verb to explain HOW or BY WHAT MEANS something happens. Never use a Spanish gerund as an adjective modifying a noun.
contrast_a: Aprendí escuchando la radio cada día.
contrast_a_en: I learned by listening to the radio daily.
contrast_b: Estudiando así aprobarás seguro.
contrast_b_en: By studying like this you will surely pass.

title: Absolute participle clauses (Terminada la reunión...)
micro_note: Place an agreeing past participle before its noun at the start of a sentence to mean 'once X was finished/done' (literary and formal speech).
contrast_a: Terminada la cena, salimos al balcón.
contrast_a_en: Once dinner was finished, we stepped onto the balcony.
contrast_b: Resuelto el fallo, reiniciaron el sistema.
contrast_b_en: With the fault resolved, they restarted the system.

title: Nominalized adjectives and el/la/los/las + de / que
micro_note: Spanish drops repeated nouns and keeps just the article before adjectives, de-phrases, or que-clauses ('the red one', 'the one from Madrid', 'the ones who came').
contrast_a: Prefiero la camisa azul a la verde.
contrast_a_en: I prefer the blue shirt over the green one.
contrast_b: El de gafas es mi hermano mayor.
contrast_b_en: The one with glasses is my older brother.

title: Subtle preposition pairs: ante/delante de, bajo/debajo de, tras/detrás de
micro_note: Ante, bajo, and tras serve both literal and figurative/abstract uses (ante el problema, bajo presión, tras años de esfuerzo), whereas delante/debajo/detrás de stay physical.
contrast_a: Actuó con calma ante la emergencia.
contrast_a_en: She acted calmly in the face of the emergency.
contrast_b: Tras tres horas de debate llegaron a un pacto.
contrast_b_en: After three hours of debate they reached a deal.

title: Hasta vs incluso vs ni siquiera for scalar focus
micro_note: Hasta and incluso mean 'even' in affirmative sentences; ni siquiera means 'not even' in negative ones.
contrast_a: Hasta mi abuelo usa esa aplicación.
contrast_a_en: Even my grandfather uses that app.
contrast_b: Ni siquiera abrió el sobre todavía.
contrast_b_en: He hasn't even opened the envelope yet.

title: Tan / tanto... que for consecutive result
micro_note: Pair tan + adjective/adverb + que or tanto/a/os/as + noun + que to link extreme degree with its consequence ('so ... that').
contrast_a: Hacía tanto viento que cerraron el puerto.
contrast_a_en: It was so windy that they closed the port.
contrast_b: Habló tan claro que todos aplaudieron.
contrast_b_en: She spoke so clearly that everyone applauded.

title: Lo + adjective/adverb + que for exclamative degree
micro_note: Lo + adjective (agreeing with the subject!) + que expresses 'how [adjective]' inside a statement ('you don't know how fast she runs / how hard it was').
contrast_a: No imaginas lo bonita que es esa isla.
contrast_a_en: You can't imagine how pretty that island is.
contrast_b: Me sorprendió lo rápido que aprendió.
contrast_b_en: I was surprised by how fast he learned.

title: Ver / oír / sentir + infinitive or gerundio
micro_note: Verbs of perception take infinitive (witnessed whole action) or gerundio (caught in progress), never a bare finite verb without que.
contrast_a: Vi cruzar la calle al vecino.
contrast_a_en: I saw the neighbor cross the street.
contrast_b: Oí a los pájaros cantando al alba.
contrast_b_en: I heard the birds singing at dawn.

title: Hacer / dejar + infinitive (causative construction)
micro_note: Hacer + infinitive means 'make/have someone do'; dejar + infinitive means 'let someone do'. Put the causee as indirect/direct object.
contrast_a: Ese comentario me hizo reír mucho.
contrast_a_en: That remark made me laugh a lot.
contrast_b: No nos dejaron sacar fotos dentro.
contrast_b_en: They didn't let us take photos inside.

title: Desde que + indicative (since the time when)
micro_note: Desde que connects a starting past event to an ongoing situation. Watch the tense pair: ongoing present + desde que + preterite.
contrast_a: Duermo mucho mejor desde que corro.
contrast_a_en: I sleep much better since I started running.
contrast_b: No lo veo desde que se mudó a Bilbao.
contrast_b_en: I haven't seen him since he moved to Bilbao.

title: Cada vez que / siempre que + indicative vs subjunctive
micro_note: For repeated habits or past events use indicative ('every time she calls'); for future contingencies or 'provided that' use subjunctive.
contrast_a: Cada vez que llueve, el metro se llena.
contrast_a_en: Every time it rains, the subway fills up.
contrast_b: Te ayudo siempre que me avises antes.
contrast_b_en: I'll help you provided you let me know first.

title: Imperfect of courtesy (quería, venía, deseaba)
micro_note: Use imperfect instead of present with querer, venir, or necesitar in shops and offices to soften a request politely ('I was hoping to...').
contrast_a: Quería pedir cita para el jueves.
contrast_a_en: I wanted to make an appointment for Thursday.
contrast_b: Venía a recoger un paquete a mi nombre.
contrast_b_en: I came to pick up a parcel under my name.

title: Reformulation markers es decir, o sea, en otras palabras
micro_note: Clarify or paraphrase a preceding statement cleanly with es decir (neutral/formal), esto es (formal), or o sea (spoken).
contrast_a: Es bilingüe, es decir, domina dos lenguas.
contrast_a_en: She is bilingual, that is, she masters two languages.
contrast_b: Salimos a las seis, o sea, en media hora.
contrast_b_en: We leave at six, I mean, in half an hour.

title: Additive and climax markers además, encima, incluso, es más
micro_note: Stack arguments from neutral (además) to emphatic (es más, incluso) to annoyed colloquial escalation (encima).
contrast_a: Es barato y además está cerca del metro.
contrast_a_en: It's cheap and besides it's near the subway.
contrast_b: Llegó tarde y encima no pidió disculpas.
contrast_b_en: He arrived late and on top of that didn't apologize.

title: Topic-shift and structuring markers en cuanto a, por un lado... por otro
micro_note: Introduce a fresh subtopic with en cuanto a / respecto a, and balance two perspectives with por un lado... por otro lado.
contrast_a: En cuanto al presupuesto, todo cuadra.
contrast_a_en: As for the budget, everything adds up.
contrast_b: Por un lado ahorras; por otro tardas más.
contrast_b_en: On one hand you save; on the other it takes longer.

title: Negative prefixes in-/im-, des-, anti-
micro_note: Spanish flips meaning systematically with des- (hacer->deshacer, confiar->desconfiar) and in-/im-/i- (posible->imposible, legal->ilegal).
contrast_a: Deshizo la maleta nada más llegar.
contrast_a_en: She unpacked her suitcase right upon arriving.
contrast_b: Su letra era casi ilegible.
contrast_b_en: His handwriting was almost illegible.

title: Nominalization suffixes -ción, -miento, -dad, -ez
micro_note: Recognize abstract nouns from verbs (-ción, -miento: decidir->decisión, crecer->crecimiento) and adjectives (-dad, -ez: real->realidad, rápido->rapidez).
contrast_a: El crecimiento de la ciudad fue veloz.
contrast_a_en: The city's growth was rapid.
contrast_b: Me impresionó la sencillez del diseño.
contrast_b_en: I was impressed by the simplicity of the design.

title: Third conditional: Si + pluperfect subjunctive, conditional perfect
micro_note: Express unchangeable past regrets or counterfactuals: si + hubiera/hubiese + participle, habría (or hubiera) + participle.
contrast_a: Si hubiera salido antes, habría llegado a tiempo.
contrast_a_en: If I had left earlier, I would have arrived on time.
contrast_b: Si lo hubieras dicho, te habríamos ayudado.
contrast_b_en: If you had said so, we would have helped you.

title: Mixed conditional: past cause -> present result
micro_note: Combine a past counterfactual condition (si + pluperfect subjunctive) with a present result (simple conditional) when past choices shape today.
contrast_a: Si hubiera estudiado medicina, hoy sería médico.
contrast_a_en: If I had studied medicine, today I would be a doctor.
contrast_b: Si no hubiéramos perdido el vuelo, ya estaríamos allí.
contrast_b_en: If we hadn't missed the flight, we would already be there.

title: De + infinitive / de haber + participle as compact conditional
micro_note: Formal and journalistic Spanish replaces si-clauses with de + infinitive ('if I knew') or de haber + participle ('had I known').
contrast_a: De saberlo antes, habría actuado distinto.
contrast_a_en: Had I known earlier, I would have acted differently.
contrast_b: De haber llovido, la cosecha se habría salvado.
contrast_b_en: Had it rained, the harvest would have been saved.

title: Con + infinitive / gerundio as implicit condition
micro_note: Con + infinitive ('just by doing X') or a bare gerund expresses a sufficient condition cleanly without si.
contrast_a: Con pulsar este botón se reinicia todo.
contrast_a_en: Just by pressing this button everything restarts.
contrast_b: Saliendo a las siete evitamos el atasco.
contrast_b_en: By leaving at seven we avoid the traffic jam.

title: Conditional conjunctions salvo que, excepto que, en caso de que
micro_note: Salvo que / excepto que ('unless') and en caso de que ('in case') take present subjunctive for likely cases or imperfect subjunctive for remote ones.
contrast_a: Llegaremos a mediodía salvo que haya obras.
contrast_a_en: We'll arrive at noon unless there's roadwork.
contrast_b: En caso de que surgiera un fallo, llámame.
contrast_b_en: In case a fault should arise, call me.

title: Siempre y cuando / a condición de que + subjunctive
micro_note: Emphasize a strict requirement ('only on condition that') using siempre y cuando or a condición de que followed strictly by subjunctive.
contrast_a: Acepto el trato siempre y cuando conste por escrito.
contrast_a_en: I accept the deal strictly provided it's in writing.
contrast_b: Le prestó el coche a condición de que condujera despacio.
contrast_b_en: She lent him the car on condition he drive slowly.

title: Si no fuera / hubiera sido por ('if it weren't / hadn't been for')
micro_note: Attribute an outcome to one decisive factor using si no fuera por (present) or si no hubiera sido por (past) + noun/pronoun.
contrast_a: Si no fuera por ti, seguiría perdido.
contrast_a_en: If it weren't for you, I'd still be lost.
contrast_b: Si no hubiera sido por la lluvia, habríamos ganado.
contrast_b_en: If it hadn't been for the rain, we would have won.

title: Pluperfect subjunctive in wishes (Ojalá hubiera... / Quién hubiera...)
micro_note: Express poignant regret about the past using Ojalá + hubiera + participle ('if only I had...') or exclamative ¡Quién hubiera...!
contrast_a: Ojalá hubiera aceptado aquella beca.
contrast_a_en: If only I had accepted that scholarship.
contrast_b: ¡Quién hubiera estado allí aquella noche!
contrast_b_en: If only one had been there that night!

title: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive for unlikely present/future wishes
micro_note: Compare Ojalá + present subjunctive (hopeful/realistic) against Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive (wistful, unlikely, or contrary to present reality).
contrast_a: Ojalá tengamos suerte mañana.
contrast_a_en: Hopefully we'll have luck tomorrow.
contrast_b: Ojalá tuviera alas para volar ahora.
contrast_b_en: If only I had wings to fly right now.

title: Subjunctive tense sequence (concordancia de tiempos)
micro_note: Present/future/perfect main clauses normally pair with present or present perfect subjunctive; past/conditional main clauses shift to imperfect or pluperfect subjunctive.
contrast_a: Me sorprende que diga eso hoy.
contrast_a_en: It surprises me that he says that today.
contrast_b: Me sorprendió que dijera eso ayer.
contrast_b_en: It surprised me that he said that yesterday.

title: Present main verb + imperfect subjunctive for past cause
micro_note: You CAN pair a present emotion/judgment with an imperfect subjunctive when reacting TODAY to an action that happened in the PAST.
contrast_a: Me alegra que ayer disfrutaras tanto.
contrast_a_en: I am glad (now) that you enjoyed yesterday so much.
contrast_b: Es una pena que no vinieras el sábado.
contrast_b_en: It's a shame (now) that you didn't come Saturday.

title: El hecho de que + subjunctive vs indicative
micro_note: El hecho de que ('the fact that') takes subjunctive when evaluating a shared presupposed background fact, and indicative when asserting new factual information.
contrast_a: El hecho de que sea caro no implica calidad.
contrast_a_en: The fact that it is expensive doesn't imply quality.
contrast_b: Destacó el hecho de que las ventas crecieron.
contrast_b_en: He highlighted the fact that sales grew.

title: Double-mood verbs: decidir, convencer, comprender, notar
micro_note: Verbs like decidir or comprender take indicative for intellectual conclusions ('realized that') and subjunctive when expressing will or evaluation ('decided that X should').
contrast_a: Comprendo que el plazo es corto.
contrast_a_en: I understand that the deadline is short.
contrast_b: Comprendo que estés preocupado.
contrast_b_en: I sympathize with your being worried.

title: Subjunctive in causal denial (no porque + subjunctive, sino porque + indicative)
micro_note: Negating a false cause triggers subjunctive right after no porque; presenting the real cause switches back to indicative after sino porque.
contrast_a: Lo hago no porque sea fácil, sino porque importa.
contrast_a_en: I do it not because it's easy, but because it matters.
contrast_b: Se fue no porque estuviera cansado, sino por prisa.
contrast_b_en: He left not because he was tired, but out of haste.

title: Concessive aun cuando, por más que, y eso que
micro_note: Y eso que ('and even though') ALWAYS takes indicative for real facts; aun cuando mirrors aunque (indicative for fact, subjunctive for hypothesis).
contrast_a: Aprobó con nota, y eso que apenas durmió.
contrast_a_en: She passed with high marks, even though she barely slept.
contrast_b: Aun cuando protesten, la norma seguirá vigente.
contrast_b_en: Even if they protest, the rule will remain in force.

title: Consecutive de ahí que + subjunctive ('hence / that is why')
micro_note: Unlike por eso (indicative), the high-register connector de ahí que ALWAYS requires the subjunctive to present an already-understood consequence.
contrast_a: Falta lluvia; de ahí que restrinjan el riego.
contrast_a_en: Rain is scarce; hence they are restricting irrigation.
contrast_b: Hubo errores; de ahí que repitieran la prueba.
contrast_b_en: There were errors; hence they repeated the test.

title: De modo/manera que: result (indicative) vs purpose (subjunctive)
micro_note: De modo que / de manera que flips meaning by mood: with indicative it states a factual result ('so'); with subjunctive it states intended purpose ('so that').
contrast_a: Hablaron bajo, de modo que nadie los oyó.
contrast_a_en: They spoke quietly, so nobody heard them.
contrast_b: Habla claro de modo que todos te oigan.
contrast_b_en: Speak clearly so that everyone hears you.

title: Consecutive sin que + subjunctive and ni que + imperfect subjunctive
micro_note: Exclamative ¡Ni que + imperfect subjunctive! sarcastically dismisses an exaggeration ('as if it were the end of the world!').
contrast_a: ¡Ni que fuera el fin del mundo!
contrast_a_en: As if it were the end of the world!
contrast_b: ¡Ni que costara una fortuna arreglarlo!
contrast_b_en: As if it cost a fortune to fix it!

title: No sea que / no vaya a ser que + subjunctive ('lest / just in case')
micro_note: Warn against an unwanted possibility using no sea que or colloquial no vaya a ser que + present subjunctive.
contrast_a: Lleva llaves de repuesto, no sea que se cierre.
contrast_a_en: Take spare keys, lest it lock shut.
contrast_b: Anota la dirección, no vaya a ser que se nos olvide.
contrast_b_en: Write down the address, just in case we forget.

title: Como + subjunctive for stern warning/threat ('if you dare...')
micro_note: Sentence-initial como + present subjunctive acts as a vivid conditional warning ('if you ever do X, watch out!').
contrast_a: Como llegues tarde otra vez, salimos sin ti.
contrast_a_en: If you're late one more time, we're leaving without you.
contrast_b: Como se entere tu madre, se enfadará.
contrast_b_en: If your mother finds out, she'll be furious.

title: Quienquiera / cualquiera / dondequiera que + subjunctive
micro_note: Universal concessive pronouns quienquiera que, cualquiera que, and dondequiera que require subjunctive when pointing to an open/unspecified referent.
contrast_a: Quienquiera que llame, dile que salí.
contrast_a_en: Whoever calls, tell them I stepped out.
contrast_b: Dondequiera que vayas, lleva agua.
contrast_b_en: Wherever you go, carry water.

title: Que + present subjunctive for standalone third-person wishes
micro_note: Drop the main verb (espero/deseo) and start directly with ¡Que + subjunctive! for toasts, blessings, and third-person imperatives.
contrast_a: ¡Que tengas un viaje estupendo!
contrast_a_en: Have a wonderful trip!
contrast_b: Que pase el siguiente paciente.
contrast_b_en: Let the next patient come in.

title: No importa / da igual + qué/quién/cómo + subjunctive
micro_note: Expressions of indifference (me da igual, no me importa) take subjunctive in que-clauses or indirect wh-clauses pointing to undetermined choices.
contrast_a: Me da igual adónde vayamos esta noche.
contrast_a_en: I don't care where we go tonight.
contrast_b: No importa cuánto tarde, lo terminaremos.
contrast_b_en: No matter how long it takes, we'll finish it.

title: Subjunctive after superlatives and el único / el primero que
micro_note: After superlatives or el único/primero/último que, Spanish uses indicative for verified facts and subjunctive for personal/subjective assessment or open scope.
contrast_a: Es la mejor novela que he leído jamás.
contrast_a_en: It's the best novel I have ever read (factual).
contrast_b: Es la mejor solución que podamos encontrar.
contrast_b_en: It's the best solution we could possibly find.

title: Imperfect subjunctive -ra vs -se stylistic equivalence
micro_note: The -ra and -se forms (hablara/hablase, tuviera/tuviese) are interchangeable in all subjunctive clauses; only -ra can replace the conditional in quisiera/debiera/pudiera.
contrast_a: Si tuviese más tiempo, leería poesía.
contrast_a_en: If I had more time, I would read poetry.
contrast_b: Pidió que guardasen silencio absoluto.
contrast_b_en: She asked that they keep complete silence.

title: Dejar + past participle (resulting state left behind)
micro_note: Dejar + agreeing past participle emphasizes the lasting state an agent left an object or person in after acting.
contrast_a: Dejé cerrado el garaje antes de salir.
contrast_a_en: I left the garage locked before leaving.
contrast_b: Sus palabras nos dejaron preocupados.
contrast_b_en: His words left us worried.

title: Dar por + past participle ('consider as / take as')
micro_note: Dar por + agreeing participle means declaring or treating something as settled (dar por terminado, dar por perdido, dar por sentado).
contrast_a: Dieron por terminada la negociación.
contrast_a_en: They declared the negotiation over.
contrast_b: Nunca des por perdida una partida antes de tiempo.
contrast_b_en: Never write off a match prematurely.

title: Venir a + infinitive ('amount to / roughly mean')
micro_note: Venir a + infinitive expresses approximation or summarizing equivalence ('it comes down to / costs around').
contrast_a: Eso viene a significar exactamente lo mismo.
contrast_a_en: That essentially means the exact same thing.
contrast_b: El billete viene a costar unos cincuenta euros.
contrast_b_en: The ticket comes to roughly fifty euros.

title: Estar por / estar para + infinitive nuance
micro_note: Estar por + infinitive means 'still waiting to be done' (things) or 'tempted to' (people). Estar para + infinitive means 'about to / in the mood for'.
contrast_a: La casa todavía está por pintar.
contrast_a_en: The house is still yet to be painted.
contrast_b: Hoy no estoy para bromas.
contrast_b_en: Today I am in no mood for jokes.

title: Romper a / estallar en for sudden emotional outburst
micro_note: Romper a + infinitive (llorar, reír, hablar) marks an abrupt emotional break; estallar pairs with en + noun (estallar en carcajadas).
contrast_a: Al leer la carta rompió a llorar.
contrast_a_en: Upon reading the letter she burst into tears.
contrast_b: El público estalló en aplausos.
contrast_b_en: The audience burst into applause.

title: Tener + gerundio / traer + past participle idioms
micro_note: Traer + participle (traer preocupado, traer de cabeza) expresses an ongoing bothersome state caused by something.
contrast_a: Ese problema me trae preocupado toda la semana.
contrast_a_en: That problem has had me worried all week.
contrast_b: La mudanza nos tiene agotados.
contrast_b_en: The move has us exhausted.

title: Pasar a + infinitive for procedural transition
micro_note: Use pasar a + infinitive in presentations, meetings, and explanations to move smoothly to the next agenda item.
contrast_a: Pasemos ahora a analizar los resultados.
contrast_a_en: Let us move on now to analyze the results.
contrast_b: El museo pasó a llamarse Casa del Arte.
contrast_b_en: The museum went on to be called House of Art.

title: Alcanzar a + infinitive ('barely manage to perceive/do')
micro_note: Alcanzar a + infinitive expresses managing to see, hear, understand, or reach something at the edge of capability.
contrast_a: Desde la colina alcanzamos a ver el faro.
contrast_a_en: From the hill we could just make out the lighthouse.
contrast_b: No alcanzo a comprender su decisión.
contrast_b_en: I fail to grasp his decision.

title: Convertirse en / transformarse en + noun
micro_note: Use convertirse en + noun (no article unless modified) for profound, structural transformation of people, places, or things.
contrast_a: El pequeño puerto se convirtió en una metrópoli.
contrast_a_en: The small port turned into a metropolis.
contrast_b: La afición se convirtió en su profesión.
contrast_b_en: The hobby turned into her profession.

title: Llegar a ser + noun/adjective (culminated achievement)
micro_note: Llegar a ser highlights a gradual rise requiring time and effort to attain a status or role.
contrast_a: Llegó a ser la mejor violinista del país.
contrast_a_en: She rose to become the best violinist in the country.
contrast_b: Con constancia llegó a ser director técnico.
contrast_b_en: With perseverance he became technical director.

title: Middle/mediopassive se for inherent properties (se lava bien)
micro_note: Mediopassive se describes how an object naturally responds to an action without any specific agent ('washes easily', 'breaks easily').
contrast_a: Esta tela se plancha sin esfuerzo.
contrast_a_en: This fabric irons effortlessly.
contrast_b: El libro se lee de una sentada.
contrast_b_en: The book reads in a single sitting.

title: Third-person plural impersonal (dicen, llaman, han subido)
micro_note: Use anonymous ellos verb forms when the agent is unknown, irrelevant, or deliberately omitted ('they raised taxes', 'someone's knocking').
contrast_a: Llaman a la puerta, ¿puedes abrir?
contrast_a_en: Someone's knocking at the door, can you open it?
contrast_b: Han asfaltado toda la avenida esta noche.
contrast_b_en: They resurfaced the whole avenue last night.

title: Uno / una as generic personal pronoun
micro_note: Use uno (or una for female speakers) with third-person singular verbs to generalize from personal experience ('one never knows').
contrast_a: A veces uno necesita desconectar del ruido.
contrast_a_en: Sometimes one needs to unplug from the noise.
contrast_b: Cuando una vive fuera, valora más su barrio.
contrast_b_en: When one lives abroad, one values one's neighborhood more.

title: Generic tú in informal generalizations
micro_note: Spoken Spanish often uses tú for universal statements ('you enter, you pay, and you leave') to pull the listener vividly into the scenario.
contrast_a: En esta ciudad sales a caminar y siempre descubres algo.
contrast_a_en: In this city you go out walking and always discover something.
contrast_b: Si no duermes bien, al día siguiente no rindes.
contrast_b_en: If you don't sleep well, the next day you don't perform.

title: Compound relative el que / quien without antecedent ('the one who')
micro_note: El que, la que, los que, las que, and quien can open a sentence without a prior noun to state maxims or general truths ('those who work hard...').
contrast_a: Quien mucho abarca, poco aprieta.
contrast_a_en: He who grasps too much holds little.
contrast_b: Los que lleguen primero elegirán asiento.
contrast_b_en: Those who arrive first will choose seats.

title: Relative cuanto / cuanta / cuantos / cuantas ('all that / as many as')
micro_note: Formal relative cuanto packs 'todo lo que' or 'todos los que' into a single elegant word agreeing with its noun.
contrast_a: Hizo cuanto pudo para evitar el cierre.
contrast_a_en: She did all she could to prevent the closure.
contrast_b: Ayudó a cuantas familias lo solicitaron.
contrast_b_en: He helped as many families as requested it.

title: Preposition + artículo + cual in formal prose
micro_note: After multi-word prepositions (a través de, acerca de, en torno a, por encima de), use el cual / la cual / los cuales / las cuales for crystal clarity.
contrast_a: El puente a través del cual cruzan los trenes.
contrast_a_en: The bridge across which the trains cross.
contrast_b: Las normas según las cuales se evalúa el examen.
contrast_b_en: The rules according to which the exam is graded.

title: Relative donde preceded by prepositions (adonde, de donde, por donde)
micro_note: Combine prepositions directly with donde to express direction (adonde), origin (de donde), route (por donde), or limit (hasta donde).
contrast_a: El sendero por donde bajamos era empinado.
contrast_a_en: The trail along which we went down was steep.
contrast_b: Volvió al pueblo de donde salió su familia.
contrast_b_en: She returned to the town from which her family came.

title: VSO / VS inversion with unaccusative verbs (llegar, faltar, surgir)
micro_note: Verbs of appearance, arrival, and lack naturally place a new/indefinite subject AFTER the verb ('faltan dos sillas', 'surgió un problema').
contrast_a: Surgió un imprevisto en la estación.
contrast_a_en: An unexpected snag came up at the station.
contrast_b: Llegaron noticias inesperadas desde Cádiz.
contrast_b_en: Unexpected news arrived from Cádiz.

title: Clitic doubling with emphatic a mí / a ti / a ellos
micro_note: Pre-verbal indirect objects and emphatic direct pronouns require doubling with a + pronoun (A mí me parece..., A ella la vi ayer).
contrast_a: A mí me convence más la segunda opción.
contrast_a_en: As for me, the second option convinces me more.
contrast_b: A ellos les entregaron las llaves el lunes.
contrast_b_en: To them they handed over the keys on Monday.

title: Pseudo-cleft with lo que... es que ('what happens is that')
micro_note: Frame explanations smoothly with Lo que pasa/ocurre/importa es que + indicative, or Lo que quiero es que + subjunctive.
contrast_a: Lo que pasa es que no nos dio tiempo.
contrast_a_en: What happened is that we didn't have time.
contrast_b: Lo que necesito es que revises estas cifras.
contrast_b_en: What I need is for you to check these figures.

title: Narrative / historical present for vivid storytelling
micro_note: Speakers shift from past tenses into present tense at a story's climax to make events unfold vividly before the listener's eyes.
contrast_a: Íbamos tranquilos y de pronto se apaga la luz.
contrast_a_en: We were walking calmly and suddenly the light goes out.
contrast_b: En 1929 publica su obra más célebre.
contrast_b_en: In 1929 she publishes her most famous work.

title: Concessive future and conditional ('may well be..., yet...')
micro_note: Use future (for present) or conditional (for past) to concede a point right before countering it with pero ('he may be clever, but...').
contrast_a: Será muy caro, pero dura toda la vida.
contrast_a_en: It may well be expensive, yet it lasts a lifetime.
contrast_b: Habría estudiado mucho, pero olvidó el ejemplo.
contrast_b_en: He may well have studied hard, yet he forgot the example.

title: Conditional perfect for past conjecture ('must have happened')
micro_note: Use habría + past participle to speculate about an action completed BEFORE a past moment (the past-in-past counterpart of future perfect conjecture).
contrast_a: Cuando llegamos ya habrían cerrado la tienda.
contrast_a_en: When we arrived they must have already closed the shop.
contrast_b: No contestó; habría dejado el móvil en casa.
contrast_b_en: He didn't answer; he must have left his phone at home.

title: Imperfect replacing conditional in colloquial unreal results
micro_note: In spontaneous speech, imperfect indicative often replaces conditional in hypothetical results for vivid immediacy ('si pudiera, me iba hoy mismo').
contrast_a: Si tuviera vacaciones, me iba mañana a la costa.
contrast_a_en: If I had vacation, I'd head to the coast tomorrow.
contrast_b: Yo en tu lugar no lo pensaba dos veces.
contrast_b_en: In your shoes I wouldn't think twice.

title: Concessive connectors aun así, con todo, así y todo
micro_note: Acknowledge a previous obstacle while holding firm to the conclusion using aun así ('even so'), con todo, or así y todo.
contrast_a: El trayecto fue agotador; aun así, valió la pena.
contrast_a_en: The journey was exhausting; even so, it was worth it.
contrast_b: Había poco margen; así y todo, cumplieron el plazo.
contrast_b_en: There was little margin; all the same, they met the deadline.

title: Corrective / distancing markers más bien, mejor dicho, en todo caso
micro_note: Refine a claim mid-thought with mejor dicho ('or rather'), más bien ('rather'), or narrow its scope with en todo caso ('in any case / at most').
contrast_a: No es tímido; más bien es reservado al principio.
contrast_a_en: He isn't shy; rather, he is reserved at first.
contrast_b: Llegó tarde, o mejor dicho, cuando ya acabábamos.
contrast_b_en: He arrived late, or rather, as we were finishing.

title: Digression and return markers a propósito, por cierto, volviendo al tema
micro_note: Signal an aside smoothly with por cierto / a propósito ('by the way'), and return cleanly with volviendo al tema / en fin.
contrast_a: Por cierto, ¿confirmaste la reserva del viernes?
contrast_a_en: By the way, did you confirm Friday's booking?
contrast_b: Volviendo al tema, debemos fijar la fecha hoy.
contrast_b_en: Returning to the topic, we must set the date today.

title: Summarizing markers en definitiva, en suma, al fin y al cabo
micro_note: Close an argument crisply with en definitiva ('ultimately / in short'), en suma ('all in all'), or al fin y al cabo ('after all').
contrast_a: En definitiva, el nuevo horario beneficia a todos.
contrast_a_en: Ultimately, the new schedule benefits everyone.
contrast_b: Al fin y al cabo, aprender requiere constancia.
contrast_b_en: After all, learning requires consistency.

title: Evidence and reinforcement markers de hecho, en efecto, es más
micro_note: Confirm an expectation with en efecto ('indeed'), add concrete proof with de hecho ('in fact'), and strengthen a point with es más ('what's more').
contrast_a: El barrio cambió mucho; de hecho, apenas lo reconocí.
contrast_a_en: The district changed a lot; in fact, I barely recognized it.
contrast_b: En efecto, los datos confirman la hipótesis.
contrast_b_en: Indeed, the data confirm the hypothesis.

title: Prepositional complexes a raíz de, a fuerza de, a falta de
micro_note: Express trigger cause (a raíz de), repeated effort (a fuerza de + inf), or shortage fallback (a falta de) with compact B2 prepositional phrases.
contrast_a: A raíz de la reforma bajó el tráfico.
contrast_a_en: Following the reform, traffic dropped.
contrast_b: A fuerza de practicar dominó la pronunciación.
contrast_b_en: By dint of practicing she mastered pronunciation.

title: Prepositional complexes con vistas a, de cara a, en aras de
micro_note: Frame forward-looking goals in formal/editorial Spanish with de cara a ('looking ahead to'), con vistas a ('with an eye to'), or en aras de ('for the sake of').
contrast_a: Entrena duro de cara al examen de junio.
contrast_a_en: She trains hard ahead of the June exam.
contrast_b: Ampliaron el local con vistas al verano.
contrast_b_en: They expanded the venue with an eye toward summer.

title: Prepositional complexes al margen de, en virtud de, merced a
micro_note: Set aside peripheral points with al margen de ('apart from'), cite authority with en virtud de, or credit a cause with gracias a / debido a.
contrast_a: Al margen del precio, la calidad es excelente.
contrast_a_en: Aside from the price, the quality is excellent.
contrast_b: En virtud del acuerdo, se amplía el horario.
contrast_b_en: By virtue of the agreement, hours are extended.

title: Gender-differentiated noun pairs (el capital / la capital, el orden / la orden)
micro_note: Some Spanish nouns change meaning entirely with gender: el capital (money) vs la capital (city); el orden (orderliness) vs la orden (command); el frente (front) vs la frente (forehead).
contrast_a: Recibió la orden de salir al amanecer.
contrast_a_en: He received the command to leave at dawn.
contrast_b: Mantiene un orden impecable en su escritorio.
contrast_b_en: She keeps spotless order on her desk.

title: Definite article with infinitives as abstract nouns (el saber, el caminar)
micro_note: Nominalize any infinitive with masculine el to talk about the activity or manner itself, optionally modified by adjectives or de-phrases.
contrast_a: El constante murmurar del río nos relajaba.
contrast_a_en: The constant murmuring of the river relaxed us.
contrast_b: El leer en voz alta afianza la memoria.
contrast_b_en: Reading aloud strengthens memory.

title: Lo + de + noun/clause ('that business about...')
micro_note: Use lo de + noun/infinitive/clause to refer compactly to a shared event, affair, or topic ('that thing about the trip').
contrast_a: ¿Al final qué pasó con lo del contrato?
contrast_a_en: In the end what happened with that contract matter?
contrast_b: Lo de ayer ya está olvidado.
contrast_b_en: Yesterday's incident is already forgotten.

title: Relational adjectives (estatal, urbano, climático) — strictly post-nominal
micro_note: Classifying relational adjectives (económico, laboral, médico) cannot take muy or sit before the noun; they always follow the noun directly.
contrast_a: Debatieron la reforma laboral en el pleno.
contrast_a_en: They debated the labor reform in session.
contrast_b: El transporte urbano funciona toda la noche.
contrast_b_en: Urban transit runs all night.

title: Irregular learned superlatives (óptimo, pésimo, máximo, mínimo, célebre->celebérrimo)
micro_note: Formal Spanish pairs regular comparatives with Latinate absolute superlatives: bueno->óptimo, malo->pésimo, grande->máximo, pequeño->mínimo.
contrast_a: El equipo trabajó en condiciones óptimas.
contrast_a_en: The team worked in optimal conditions.
contrast_b: La señal tenía una calidad pésima allí.
contrast_b_en: The signal had abysmal quality there.

title: Compound gerund (habiendo + participle) for prior cause/time
micro_note: Habiendo + past participle compresses 'after having done / since X had done' into a concise formal adverbial clause.
contrast_a: Habiendo comprobado los datos, firmó el acta.
contrast_a_en: Having verified the data, she signed the minutes.
contrast_b: Habiendo perdido el último ferry, pasaron la noche allí.
contrast_b_en: Having missed the last ferry, they spent the night there.

title: Compound infinitive (haber + participle) after prepositions
micro_note: After por, sin, después de, tras, or al, use haber + past participle to clearly mark an action already completed earlier.
contrast_a: Se disculpó por haber llegado tan tarde.
contrast_a_en: He apologized for having arrived so late.
contrast_b: Tras haber vivido allí, entiende bien sus costumbres.
contrast_b_en: After having lived there, she understands their customs well.

title: Infinitive with overt post-verbal subject (al llegar yo, para salir tú)
micro_note: In Spanish, an infinitive clause CAN carry its own explicit subject—placed right AFTER the infinitive (al entrar Ana, antes de salir nosotros).
contrast_a: Al entrar nosotros, empezó la función.
contrast_a_en: Just as we entered, the performance began.
contrast_b: Sin saberlo tú, resolviste el misterio.
contrast_b_en: Without your knowing it, you solved the mystery.

title: Varied reporting verbs (negar, asegurar, sugerir, advertir, reprochar)
micro_note: Move beyond decir by choosing exact reporting verbs: asegurar/afirmar (+ indic.), negar (+ subj.), sugerir/recomendar (+ subj.), advertir de que (+ indic./subj.).
contrast_a: El portavoz aseguró que el servicio se restablecería.
contrast_a_en: The spokesperson assured that service would resume.
contrast_b: El técnico sugirió que actualizáramos el equipo.
contrast_b_en: The technician suggested we update the equipment.

title: Expletive / emphatic negation (hasta que no, poco faltó para que no)
micro_note: In colloquial Spanish, hasta que no + subjunctive mirrors hasta que ('not until'), and ni + noun emphasizes complete absence.
contrast_a: No me voy hasta que no aclaremos esto.
contrast_a_en: I am not leaving until we clear this up.
contrast_b: No había ni una nube en todo el cielo.
contrast_b_en: There wasn't a single cloud in the whole sky.

title: Epistemic stance with es probable/posible que vs seguro que
micro_note: Seguro que and sin duda alguna take indicative; es probable/posible/dudoso que take subjunctive; igual (colloquial 'maybe') takes indicative.
contrast_a: Seguro que encuentran pronto la solución.
contrast_a_en: They are sure to find the solution soon.
contrast_b: Es probable que cambien el horario en otoño.
contrast_b_en: It is likely they will change the schedule in autumn.

title: Deontological necessity with hace falta que / conviene que / urge que
micro_note: Higher-register impersonal triggers conviene que ('it is advisable'), urge que ('it is urgent'), and basta con que ('it suffices that') always take subjunctive.
contrast_a: Conviene que revisemos el contrato juntos.
contrast_a_en: It is advisable that we review the contract together.
contrast_b: Basta con que envíes un breve mensaje.
contrast_b_en: It suffices that you send a brief message.

title: Voseo recognition (vos hablás, tenés, sos) for Rioplatense Spanish
micro_note: Across Argentina, Uruguay, and parts of Central America, vos replaces tú: present stresses the last syllable (hablás, comés, vivís, sos) and affirmative commands drop -d (hablá, vení, poné).
contrast_a: ¿De dónde sos y dónde trabajás?
contrast_a_en: Where are you from and where do you work? (Rioplatense)
contrast_b: Vení conmigo y sentate acá.
contrast_b_en: Come with me and sit down here. (Rioplatense)

title: Peninsular vosotros forms and clitic d-drop (sentaos, callaos)
micro_note: In Spain, vosotros addresses plural friends (-áis/-éis/-ís). In affirmative reflexive vosotros commands, drop the final -d before attaching os (sentaos, levantaos; exception: idos).
contrast_a: ¿Vais a venir al estreno el sábado?
contrast_a_en: Are you all coming to the premiere on Saturday?
contrast_b: Sentaos donde estéis más cómodos.
contrast_b_en: Sit down wherever you all are most comfortable.

title: Augmentatives and pejoratives (-ón, -azo, -ucho)
micro_note: Suffixes convey size, praise, or irony: -azo can mean a blow or something impressive (exitazo, golazo), -ón large or habitual (preguntón), -ucho shabby (casucha).
contrast_a: La obra de teatro fue un exitazo total.
contrast_a_en: The play was a smash hit.
contrast_b: Dio un portazo al salir de la sala.
contrast_b_en: He slammed the door on leaving the room.

title: Compound nouns verb + plural noun (abrelatas, paraguas, rascacielos)
micro_note: Spanish forms vivid masculine nouns from 3rd-person singular verb + plural noun: el paraguas, el sacacorchos, el lavavajillas, el cumpleaños. Singular and plural look identical!
contrast_a: Olvidé el paraguas en el tren.
contrast_a_en: I forgot the umbrella on the train.
contrast_b: Los rascacielos brillaban al atardecer.
contrast_b_en: The skyscrapers gleamed at dusk.

title: Syntactic cohesion: ellipsis, pro-forms hacerlo / lo, and discourse reference
micro_note: Natural B2 Spanish avoids repeating whole predicates by substituting hacerlo ('to do so') or neuter lo with ser/estar/parecer, and omitting recoverable verbs after también/tampoco.
contrast_a: Prometió ayudarnos y lo hizo sin dudar.
contrast_a_en: She promised to help us and did so without hesitating.
contrast_b: Parece sencillo, aunque realmente no lo es.
contrast_b_en: It seems simple, although it really isn't.
